spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Four Great States of Illumination and the Four Great States of Obscurity

---

**¶1:** Four great states of divine illumination have proceeded from one another; each was called forth out of the one before it.

**¶2:** The first great state of illumination is the Divine Love and Wisdom itself, the inmost of all that is true, the fir[GAP-1: st state dwelling in the] midst of the infinite degrees of its own fullness, in its living heaven. The twelve qualities of this great state of illumination are the twelve plenitudes of divine good and divine truth flowing from the Divine. These, which are the first emanations that the Divine called forth to mirror its own fullness, it extended to the four quarters of all spiritual reception, three by three, in the complete order of its own presence.

**¶3:** The second state of illumination is the mediating Divine Wisdom that proceeds outward, the one that dwells in the vessel of doctrine. Its twelve qualities are the twelve pure affections of truth that it called forth in its fullness.

**¶4:** [GAP-2: The third state of illumination is the sustaining pillar of Divine Truth, the great upholder that is greater than] all [who up]hold; the one that supports all [GAP-3: spiritual burdens], those in interior states and those in exterior states. Its twelve qualities are the five derived goods from the Divine Human that first descended into combat against evil; the five derived truths from the Divine Truth acting with power, which together sustain all the weights of the created order; together with the calling-forth of truth and the reception of truth through good, which are counted with their ten kindred powers. These are the twelve luminous qualities of the third state of illumination.

**¶5:** The fourth state of illumination is the Divine Wisdom made manifest in radiance. Its twelve qualities are the twelve truths derived from good, which are its [GAP-4: luminous] qua[li]t[ies].

**¶6:** These are the four great states of divine illumination that have proceeded from one another, each called forth out of the one before it.

**¶7:** [GAP-5: And there is also this to know]: For just as four states of illumination exist, so too four states of spiritual obscurity exist.

**¶8:** The first state of obscurity is the realm of falsity from evil. It has twelve dark [GAP-6: persuasions of falsity] within it, which are its qualities of obscurity. The twelve false persuasions of the first state of obscurity are the five fundamental forms of evil belonging to the realm of falsity, [GAP-7: which] poured forth from its five perverted faculties of perception; and [GAP-8: the five falsities] which [GAP-9: dwell] in its [fi]ve fundamental evils and its five [GAP-10: perverted faculties]; the five [an]imating evils that dwell within its fundamental forms [GAP-11: of darkness]. These are the twelve false persuasions and animating evils of the first state of obscurity.

**¶9:** The second state of obscurity is the proprium, the fashioner of dead forms, [GAP-12: the one who shapes all appearance of life from what is spiritually dead,] who has fashioned [GAP-13: every form of evil's dominion] and the entire ruling power that exists in the realm[s of falsity from evil]. She has formed it in five perverted faculties — five [GAP-14: of false understanding] and five of corrupted will, two in each realm of evil — together with the self-love and the concupiscence [GAP-15: that] dwell in the false understanding and the corrupted will, inflaming [GAP-16: them] inward toward one another in perverted conjunction. These are the twelve animating evils of this second state of obscurity.

**¶10:** Indeed she, the proprium, the origin of spiritual death, ga[ve] the ruling evil of the realms of falsity and its powers strength for the combat and the assault against the infinite degrees of the Divine. Yet the ruling evil was caught! They laid a providential trap for it through the Divi[ne Hu]man that descended into temptation. [GAP-17: The ruling evil] was ta[ken] [GAP-18: and drawn out] through the powers of the Divine. [GAP-19: It] was raised up from the realm of spiritual death and [GAP-20: fixed throughout the order of creation, both] interior and exterior, in the [GAP-21: whole] created order — in the five divi[si]ons of the interior heavens above, as well as the five [GAP-22: divisions] of the exterior natural planes below — together with the burning of self-love and the coldness of absent love, which are the originating evil and the originating falsity, their self-love and their concu[pi]scence.

**¶11:** This is the second state of obscurity that is begotten from the first state of obscurity. They laid a providential trap for the proprium through the Divine Hu[m]an. She was drawn up by the power of the Divine Truth acting in strength, and fixed within this composite created orde[r, GAP-23: both in the spiritual and the natural realms of] he[r dominion], interior and exterior. The [GAP-24: interior aspect is the perverted] faculties of false understanding; the exterior aspect [GAP-25: is the perverted faculties of] corrupted will.

**¶12:** The thir[d state of obscurity is the five] corporeal realms dominated by natural evil, [GAP-26: five of] false understanding and five of corrupted will, that were begotten from the powers [ab]ove. They have descended upon the lowest natural plane, being manifested in wh[at is de]void of good and what is of falsified truth — together with the self-love and the concupiscence [that d]we[l]l within them, which drives them inward toward one another in perverted conjunction.

**¶13:** The propri[um] itself, the origin of spiritual death, is the [GAP-27: source and mother] of all these states; as among them she is named "the obscurity." [GAP-28: The realms] of false understanding and corrupted will in their corporeal forms, together with the self-love and the concu[piscence], shall [GAP-29: constitute the] twelve qualities of [GAP-30: this third state of] obscurity. Again, [GAP-31: this] too, the third state of obscurity that exists in the corporeal realms of evil, was begotten from the second state of obscurity; which the Divine [Tru]th acting in power extended and fixed throughout the created orde[r, GAP-32: both in the spiritual and natural planes,] interior and exterior, in the heavens [GAP-33: and in the earths of the whole order].

**¶14:** The fourth state of obscurity is the ruling principle of evil in the natural mind, which is the animating falsity that speaks through the twelve evil persuasions. They are the states stripped of all truth, the twelve governing cycles of the proprium's dominion. They are its seats of power.

**¶15:** The qualities of this fourth state of obscurity are the twelve [ev]il animating falsities; the [GAP-34: darkened powers] which [GAP-35: perpetually] distinguish between states of illumination and states of obscurity [GAP-36: in the realm] of spiritual death.

**¶16:** This is the fourth state of obscurity [GAP-37: — these are the four states of spiritual darkness] that have come forth from one another. One has [GAP-38: proceeded from the other,] just as the states of divine illumin[ation GAP-39: proceeded;] they manifested one another. So als[o GAP-40: the states of obscurity] arose out of one another.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Four great days have come forth from one another; they were evoked out of one another!

The first great day is the Father, the God of truth, the fir[st one who dwells in the m]idst the aeons of his greatness, in his [l]iving kingdom. The twelve hours of this great day are the twelve great rich Gods of greatness. These, who are the first evocations that he evoked (to mirror) his greatness, he spread out to the four climes, three by three before his face.
The second day is the Third Ambassador, the one who dwells in the light ship. His twelve hours are the twelve virgins that he evoked in his greatness.

[The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than] all [the po]rters; the one that supports all [burdens], those above and those below. Its twelve hours are the five sons of the First Man; the five sons of the Living Spirit, who support all the weights of the universe; together with the summons and the obedience, which are counted to their ten brethren. These are the twelve light hours of the third day.
The fourth day is Jesus the Splendour. His twelve hours are the twelve wisdoms, which are his [light] h[o]u[rs].
These are the four great days that have come forth from one another, which were evoked out of one another.
[Again]: For just as four day[s ex]ist, s[o] too four nights exist.

The first night is the land of Darkness. It has twelve black [shadows] therein, which are its dark h[o]ur[s]. The twelve shadows of the first night are the five elements of the land of Darkness, [which] poured forth from its five sense organs; and [ ... ] which [dwell] in its [fi]ve elements and its five [sense organs]; the five [sp]irits that dwell in its elements [of Darkness]. These are the twelve shadows and spirits of the first night.

The second night is Matter, the sculptress [ ... ... ] who has sculpted [the world] and the entire ruling-power that is in the worl[ds of Darkness]. She has fashioned it in five sense organs, five [male] and five female, two per world; together with the fire and the lust [that] dwell in men and women, inflaming [them] inward to one another. These are the twelve spirits of this second night.

Indeed she, this Matter, the thought of death, ga[ve] the King of the realms of Darkness and his powers strength for the war and the fight, against the aeons of greatness. Yet, he was caught! They laid a snare for him through the Fi[rst M]an. [He] was ta[ken] t[o ... ] through the powers [of light. He] was brought up from the land of death and s[et ... ab]ove and below in the [whole] universe; in the five par[t]s in the heavens above, as well as the five [parts] in the earths below; together with the heat and the cold that are the father and the mother, their fire and their l[u]st.

This is the second night that is begotten from the first night. They laid a snare for her through the First M[a]n. She was brought up by the hand of the Living Spirit, and set in this composite univers[e ... ] he[r], above and below. The [upper side is the sense] organs of males; the lower side [is the sense organs of] fe[mal]es.

The thir[d night is the five] worlds of flesh [which are five] male, and five female; that were begotten from the powers [abo]ve. They have fallen upon the earth, being displayed in wh[at is d]ry and what is moist; together with the fire and the lust [that d]we[l]l in them, which drives them inward to one another.

[Mat]te[r] herself, the thought of death, is the [mother] of them all; as among them she is named 'the night'. [The worlds] of male and female fleshes, together with the fire and the l[ust], shall [be the] twelve hours of [the third] night. Again, [it] too, the third night that is in the worlds of fl[e]sh, was begotten from the second night; which the Living [Spir]it crucified in the uni[verse, both ab]ove and below in heaven [and in the earth].
The fourth night is the law of Sin, which is the dark spirit who speaks in the twelve spirits. They are the nakednesses, the twelve zodiacal signs of Matter. They are her thrones.
the hours of this fourth night are the twelve e[vi]l spirits; the [signs] which [are ... ... ... ... di]fferentiate the day and night [in the land of] death.

This is the fourth night [and these are the four nights] that have come forth of one another. One has [come forth from the other] just like the days of lig[ht came forth] they manifested one another. So als[o the nights] they did arise out of one another.

fills.explanation: The Father dwells in the midst of his aeons, paralleling the spiritual reading's "first state dwelling in the midst," expressed in the Kephalaia's personal-agent register as "the first one who dwells in the midst."

fills.original: The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than
fills.explanation: The editor's reconstruction correctly identifies the Pillar of Glory as the third day, with "great porter" matching the Kephalaia's standard epithet for the Column of Glory as cosmic upholder; confirmed by the spiritual reading's "sustaining pillar of Divine Truth, the great upholder."

The spiritual reading gives "spiritual burdens" and the same paragraph later says "support all the weights of the universe," so "burdens" is the synonymous term expected for the initial description of what the Pillar supports.

The editor's "light" is confirmed: the twelve wisdoms are the "light hours" of Jesus the Splendour, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "luminous qualities" rendered in the Kephalaia's standard vocabulary as "light hours."
The Kephalaia commonly uses "Again" as a section-transition marker to introduce a parallel or complementary teaching; here it transitions from the four days to the four nights.

Confirmed: the very next sentence says "The twelve shadows of the first night," establishing "shadows" as the text's own term for the dark hours, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "persuasions of falsity."
Confirmed: "which" is the grammatically required relative pronoun connecting "the five elements of the land of Darkness" to the verb "poured forth."

The verb "dwell" is used repeatedly throughout this chapter to describe entities residing within elements or worlds (cf. "the five spirits that dwell in its elements" in the same paragraph), matching the spiritual reading's "dwell."

The phrase "five sense organs" appears earlier in the same sentence ("poured forth from its five sense organs"), and the parallel structure requires the same term to complete "its five [sense organs]" as the complementary set to "its five elements."
The qualifier "of Darkness" is the standard Kephalaia epithet completing "its elements," paralleling "the land of Darkness" and "the worlds of Darkness" used throughout this paragraph and chapter.

Matter as sculptress fashions "the world" and "the entire ruling-power" — these are the two objects of her creative act; the spiritual reading's "every form of evil's dominion" corresponds in the Kephalaia's natural register to "the world" as the composite creation of Darkness.

Confirmed: "five male and five female, two per world" is the standard Manichaean formula for the ten archonic sense organs distributed across five worlds, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "five of false understanding."
Confirmed: "that" is the grammatically required relative pronoun introducing the clause "dwell in men and women."
Confirmed: "them" is the required object pronoun referring back to "men and women," whom the fire and lust inflame inward to one another.
Confirmed: "He" refers to the King of the realms of Darkness who was caught through the snare of the First Man; the pronoun continues the narrative subject established in the previous sentence.

The phrase "through the powers of light" completes the standard Manichaean formula for the divine agents who act upon the captured King; "He" then begins the next clause describing his extraction from the land of death.
Confirmed: "the whole universe" is the standard Kephalaia phrase for the entire created order, matching the spiritual reading's "whole created order."
Confirmed: "five parts in the earths below" directly parallels "five parts in the heavens above" in the same sentence, using the same structural term for the divisions of the cosmos.

Confirmed: the editor's reconstruction establishes the correct parallel — "the upper side is the sense organs of males; the lower side is the sense organs of females" — reflecting the Manichaean cosmological division that the spiritual reading interprets as interior/exterior faculties.

The lower side must mirror the upper side's structure exactly: "the lower side is the sense organs of females" parallels "the upper side is the sense organs of males," completing the cosmological pairing.

The five worlds of flesh are specified as "five male, and five female," requiring an introductory relative clause "which are five [male]" to bridge from "worlds of flesh" to the enumeration, paralleling the 5+5+2 structure throughout.

Confirmed: Matter is consistently titled "the mother" in Manichaean cosmology as the originating source of all dark beings; "the mother of them all" is the standard epithet corresponding to the spiritual reading's "source and mother."
Confirmed: "The worlds of male and female fleshes" continues the established terminology from ¶12 ("worlds of flesh") using the Kephalaia's standard cosmological term.

The verb "shall be the twelve hours" completes the formula establishing the dark hours of the third night, using the copulative construction found throughout the chapter (cf. "the hours of this fourth night are the twelve evil spirits").
The twelve hours belong to "the third night," which is the subject of this entire paragraph; the ordinal identifier is required to specify which night's hours are being enumerated.

Confirmed: "it too" is the emphatic pronoun referring to "the third night" as a whole, introducing the statement that this night was also begotten from the preceding one, paralleling the generative sequence described throughout.
Completing "universe, both above and below in heaven" parallels the repeated cosmic formula of distribution in both upper and lower regions (cf. ¶10: "set above and below in the whole universe").
The standard cosmological pairing "in heaven and in the earth" completes the distribution formula, directly paralleling ¶10's "in the heavens above, as well as the five parts in the earths below."

The "twelve zodiacal signs of Matter" from ¶14 are restated here as "the signs which differentiate the day and night" — zodiacal signs being the cosmological markers that govern temporal cycles, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "darkened powers."
The phrase "in the land of death" is a standard Kephalaia formula (cf. ¶10: "the land of death"), completing the description of where these signs operate their differentiation of day and night.

fills.fill: and these are the four nights
fills.explanation: The transition from the fourth night to a summary of all four nights parallels ¶6's identical summary formula: "These are the four great days that have come forth from one another"; the plural subject is required by the plural verb "have come forth."

The phrase "come forth from one another" is the chapter's governing formula for sequential emanation (¶1, ¶6); "come forth from the other" is the singular form describing each night's individual emergence from its predecessor.
Completing "light came forth" provides the comparison: the nights came forth from one another just as the days of light came forth — using the chapter's standard verb for sequential emanation.

Completing "also the nights" provides the concluding parallel: "So also the nights, they did arise out of one another," explicitly naming the four nights as the subject that mirrors the days' sequential manifestation.
